titulo: Japan Inflation Rises Above BOJ Target Level, Backing Rate Hikes
resumen: Japan’s key price gauge rose above the Bank of Japan’s target level for the first time this year, supporting the case for a widely expected BOJ interest rate hike in December.

titulo: Australia’s Victoria State Approves $700 Million Gas Project
resumen: Australia’s Victoria state has approved the production license for a A$1 billion ($700 million) natural gas project to help avoid a forecast gas shortage.

titulo: Brazil Election: Lula’s New Cell Phone Gives Him a Shot at Reelection
resumen: Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stubbornly made a point of never wanting, or needing, a cell phone. A jaw-dropping election setback made him reconsider. The question now is whether it’s too late.

titulo: OpenAI Shifts Value to $1.25 Trillion as Funding Talks Finalize
resumen: OpenAI, which is seeking to raise around $30 billion in a fresh funding round, is now targeting a valuation of $1.25 trillion during the final stages of negotiations, according to people familiar with the matter.

titulo: Nasdaq 100 Clocks Worst Day In Four Months As Investors Grow Weary Of Capex, Elevated Debt — META, SPCX, BE, MRNA In Focus
resumen: Meta’s plan to boost capex reignited investor concerns as more tech firms look to raise debt to fund AI growth.

titulo: 3 Vanguard ETFs Pay Up to 3.71%, and One Is Beating the S&P 500
resumen: Three Vanguard ETFs offer yields as high as 3.71%, but their total returns over the past year tell very different stories about which one actually rewarded patient investors and which quietly destroyed wealth despite steady payouts.

titulo: Etsy bans AI-generated recipes and patterns from its online marketplace
resumen: Etsy also laid out clearer rules around AI usage on its platform, including barring sellers from creating bot-generated listings without any human involvement.

titulo: Japan core inflation in September surges to its highest this year at 2.1%
resumen: Core inflation, which strips out prices of fresh food, was in line with than the 2.1% forecast by economists polled by Reuters.

titulo: Politicians Are Turning Against AI, but Your Pension Is Riding on It
resumen: AI-linked stocks drove $138 billion in gains across 13 public-pension funds since 2022, helping them dig out of losses from the last financial crisis.
